walmart <- read_csv("Walmart.csv") |> clean_names() 
walmart <- walmart %>%
  mutate(
    transaction_date = lubridate::mdy_hm(transaction_date),
    transaction_day  = as.Date(transaction_date)
  )
walmart$revenue <- walmart$quantity_sold * walmart$unit_price
table(walmart$category)
## 
##  Appliances Electronics 
##        2415        2585
prop.table(table(walmart$category))
## 
##  Appliances Electronics 
##       0.483       0.517
library(dplyr)
walmart %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(
    total_revenue = sum(revenue),
    mean_revenue = mean(revenue),
    median_revenue = median(revenue),
    sd_revenue = sd(revenue),
    mean_quantity = mean(quantity_sold),
    n_transactions = n()
  )
## # A tibble: 2 × 7
##   category    total_revenue mean_revenue median_revenue sd_revenue mean_quantity
##   <chr>               <dbl>        <dbl>          <dbl>      <dbl>         <dbl>
## 1 Appliances       7321970.        3032.          2322.      2368.          2.97
## 2 Electronics      7941632.        3072.          2440.      2374.          3.00
## # ℹ 1 more variable: n_transactions <int>

With this in mind now I create a boxplot of revenue by category to compare medians and visualize any outliers.

ggplot(walmart, aes(x = category, y = revenue)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Revenue Distribution by Category")

ggplot(walmart, aes(x = category, y = quantity_sold)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Quantity Sold Distribution by Category")

walmart %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(total_revenue = sum(revenue)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = category, y = total_revenue)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Total Revenue by Category")

t.test(revenue ~ category, data = walmart)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  revenue by category
## t = -0.60097, df = 4976.6, p-value = 0.5479
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group Appliances and group Electronics is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -171.87764   91.22465
## sample estimates:
##  mean in group Appliances mean in group Electronics 
##                  3031.871                  3072.198

A Welch two-sample t-test was conducted to compare mean revenue per transaction between Electronics and Appliances. The test was not statistically significant (t = -0.60, p = 0.548). The 95% confidence interval for the difference in means (-171.88, 91.22) includes zero, suggesting no meaningful difference in average revenue between the two categories.

t.test(quantity_sold ~ category, data = walmart)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  quantity_sold by category
## t = -0.6874, df = 4984.1, p-value = 0.4919
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group Appliances and group Electronics is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -0.10631955  0.05111654
## sample estimates:
##  mean in group Appliances mean in group Electronics 
##                  2.968530                  2.996132
library(effsize)
cohen.d(revenue ~ category, data = walmart)
## 
## Cohen's d
## 
## d estimate: -0.01700631 (negligible)
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##       lower       upper 
## -0.07248898  0.03847635
class(walmart$transaction_date)
## [1] "POSIXct" "POSIXt"
summary(walmart$transaction_date)
##                  Min.               1st Qu.                Median 
## "2024-01-01 00:31:00" "2024-03-07 19:21:15" "2024-05-11 20:02:30" 
##                  Mean               3rd Qu.                  Max. 
## "2024-05-11 05:10:22" "2024-07-16 08:58:15" "2024-09-16 20:22:00"
walmart <- walmart %>%
  filter(transaction_day >= as.Date("2023-12-31"),
         transaction_day <= as.Date("2024-09-16"))
walmart_month <- walmart %>%
  mutate(month = floor_date(transaction_date, "month")) %>%
  group_by(month, category) %>%
  summarise(
    total_revenue = sum(revenue),
    mean_revenue = mean(revenue),
    mean_quantity = mean(quantity_sold),
    n_transactions = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

walmart_full_months <- walmart %>%
  filter(transaction_date < as.POSIXct("2024-09-01"))
walmart_month_full <- walmart_full_months %>%
  mutate(month = floor_date(transaction_date, "month")) %>%
  group_by(month, category) %>%
  summarise(
    total_revenue = sum(revenue),
    mean_revenue = mean(revenue),
    mean_quantity = mean(quantity_sold),
    n_transactions = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(walmart_month_full, aes(x = month, y = total_revenue, color = category)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M", prefix = "$")) +
  labs(title = "Monthly Total Revenue by Category (Full Months Only)",
       x = "Month",
       y = "Revenue ($ Millions)")

last_month <- max(walmart_month_full$month)
last_month
## [1] "2024-09-01 UTC"
walmart_month_clean <- walmart_month_full %>%
  filter(month < as.Date("2024-09-01"))
ggplot(walmart_month_clean, aes(x = month, y = total_revenue, color = category)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M", prefix = "$")
  ) +
  labs(title = "Monthly Total Revenue by Category (January???August 2024)",
       x = "Month",
       y = "Revenue ($ Millions)") +
  theme_minimal()
